digest.plan:
The review is a total rejection: the story was never implemented and the implementation report presented for review was fabricated. Nothing in the digest needs re-litigating — I verified all of it against the tree. The plan is to do the work the spec describes, then author the report from the real diff and real gate output.

## 1. `src/store/verify.ts` — the parser rewrite (AC-001..AC-013)

**Tri-state contract.** Add `type BoundaryDeclaration = {kind:"none"} | {kind:"unparseable"} | {kind:"patterns", patterns: readonly string[]}` and change `declaredBoundary` (currently `string[] | undefined`, `:354`) to return it. Rewrite its doc comment, which today states the single-fence contract this replaces.

**Heading selection — fixes #135 (AC-001, AC-002).** Replace the single `lines.findIndex(...)` at `:358` with a collection of *every* index matching `/^#{1,6}\s+.*boundary/i`. Order candidates house-form-first: those whose heading text matches `/\b(frozen\s+)?pr\s+boundary\b/i` in document order, then the remainder in document order. Take the first candidate whose section yields ≥1 pattern. Candidates exist but none yields → `{kind:"unparseable"}`; no candidates or no `spec.md` → `{kind:"none"}` (EC-004). This is what stops a prose heading or an H1 title from voiding the real fence.

**`sectionPatterns(lines, headingIdx)`.** Section runs from the heading to the next heading of any level. **The scan must track fenced-block state** and ignore `#` lines inside a fence — otherwise AC-007's `# a comment` line reads as a heading and truncates the section mid-fence. (Today's code is accidentally immune because it stops heading-checking once it finds the fence start; the rewrite has to preserve that property explicitly.) Returns the union, document-ordered and de-duplicated, of the section's first fence and its first `Path` table (EC-005).

**`fencePatterns(body)` — fixes #129 (AC-006, AC-007).** Replaces `:375`'s `if (t !== "" && !t.startsWith("#"))`. Per line: trim; drop if empty; drop if it starts with `#` (whole-line comment, unchanged behaviour AC-007 pins); otherwise cut at the first `/\s+#/` — whitespace *then* `#`, so `allowed/a#b.md` survives intact — re-trim, drop if empty (EC-003). Fixes the trailing-comment entry that `boundaryRegExp` escapes into an unsatisfiable anchored regex.

**`tablePatterns(...)` (AC-003, AC-004, AC-005).** Find the section's first markdown table whose header row's first cell — trimmed, backticks and `*`/`_` emphasis stripped — equals `Path` case-insensitively. Any other first header cell (`Not here`, `Anchor`, `AC`) is **not** a declaration, which is what keeps the 9 negative-table specs from having prose turned into patterns. Skip the `---` delimiter row; from each body row's first cell take every backticked token via a global `` /`([^`]+)`/g `` and ignore all surrounding prose. Malformed tables (missing delimiter, ragged, no body rows) yield zero patterns and fall through to the next candidate — never throw (EC-001, EC-002).

**`boundaryCheck` (AC-008, AC-009, AC-010).** Add a `BOUNDARY_ADVISORY` constant naming both the problem and the remedy (heading present but nothing parseable; declare paths in a fenced block or a `| Path | Change |` table with backticked paths). Three arms: `none` → `{ran:false, pass:true, detail:"no boundary declared"}` byte-identical to today; `unparseable` → `{ran:true, pass:true, detail: BOUNDARY_ADVISORY}`, **never `pass:false`** (NF-003 — a hard fail would red ~100 specs); `patterns` → today's stray computation unchanged, `REDKILN_MANAGED` filter included. On the **failing branch only**, additionally compute declared patterns whose RegExp matched no changed file and append them (`; declared but matched no changed file: …`). A passing run stays quiet.

**`provenanceCheck` (AC-011, AC-012).** Change the `patterns === undefined` early return at `:713-715` to `declared.kind !== "patterns"`, so both `none` and `unparseable` stay `{ran:false, pass:true, detail:"no boundary declared"}` — the advisory is `boundary`'s job alone, and this keeps `test/verify.test.ts:976` green. It inherits both parse fixes for free, so a hijacked heading no longer voids the sha demand.

**`ledgerBlock` doc comment (AC-013).** Code untouched. Rewrite `:516`'s "Mirrors `declaredBoundary`'s heading→fence scan so the two behave consistently", which becomes false the moment this lands, to state and justify the divergence: the input is generated single-heading YAML with nothing to hijack, there is no table form of a ledger, and `#` must **not** be stripped because it is YAML's own comment syntax downstream in `parseYaml`.

Untouched per the spec: `boundaryRegExp` (#129 is an input defect, not a translation defect), `REDKILN_MANAGED`, `parseLedgerBlock`, `ledgerCheck`, `waiverOf`, `verifyIdentity` (its `spec=` digest already covers every byte read, so memoization stays correct — NF-004), and `src/cli/verify.ts`'s renderer (it already prints a `pass:true` check's detail, so the advisory is loud without a renderer change).

## 2. `test/verify.test.ts` — one failing test per AC, written Red first

Extend the existing fixture shape at `:220-250` (`"# Spec\n\n## PR boundary\n\n```\nallowed/\n```\n"` via `seedStory`/`gitBaseline`) rather than reinventing a harness; use `--json` and select the check by name where an AC asserts on `ran`/`pass`. New `describe` block alongside the AC-V-BOUNDARY / AC-PROV-* / AC-BOUNDARY-MANAGED suites:

- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-HIJACK** (AC-001): prose heading `### Where the chunk boundary comes from` above the real `## PR boundary` fence; stray change → exit 1, `err` matches `/changed outside declared boundary: .*stray/`, output does **not** contain `no boundary declared`.
- **AC-002**: H1 title containing "boundary", in-boundary change only → `boundary.ran === true && pass === true`.
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-TABLE** (AC-003/AC-004): house-style `## Frozen PR boundary` + `| Path | Change |` with `` `allowed/` ``; in-boundary → ran+pass; stray → exit 1 naming it.
- **AC-005**: negative `| Not here | Owner |` table only → advisory detail, `pass === true`, and the changed file is **not** reported stray (the assertion that catches prose-derived patterns).
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-COMMENT** (AC-006): two fixtures — `allowed/x.md   # only the CLI` and `allowed/a#b.md` — both admitted, exit 0 / no stray.
- **AC-007**: fence with a whole-line `# a comment` plus `allowed/` → in-boundary change passes *and* an out-of-boundary change still fails naming the stray (the regression pin the digest flagged as never written).
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-ADVISORY** (AC-008): heading with prose only → exit 0, `ran === true && pass === true`, detail matches `/nothing parseable|declares nothing/`.
- **AC-009**: `templates/spec.md`-shaped spec with no boundary heading → `ran === false` and detail exactly `no boundary declared`; `AC-PROV-BOUNDARY` at `:976` stays green unmodified.
- **AC-010**: declare `allowed/` and `never-touched/`, change only a stray → failure detail contains `never-touched/`.
- **AC-PROV-HIJACK** (AC-011): AC-001 fixture + `require_commit_provenance: true` + in-boundary change + empty `links.commits` → `err` matches `/links\.commits is empty/` and `/record-links/`.
- **AC-012**: unparseable heading + flag set → `provenance.ran === false` with the exact detail while `boundary.ran === true`.
- **AC-013**: a `#`-commented YAML line inside the ledger fence still round-trips through `parseYaml`; existing AC-LEDGER-*/waiver tests stay green unmodified.

## 3. `CHANGELOG.md`

One bullet appended to the existing `### Fixed` list under `## [Unreleased]` covering #135 and #129, explicit about NF-002: the table form makes a previously-dormant check real for the 18 active `.bklg/support/**` fix-lane specs, so a fix story that strays outside its own table now reds where it previously skipped — stated so nobody reads that new red as this fix breaking the gate. `### Pack changes / migration` stays **"None."** — this ships no pack or template change.

## 4. `dist/cli.js`, `dist/index.js`

Run `pnpm build`. `dist/` is tracked here, so without the rebuild the CLI users actually run keeps the defective parse and the capability is unreachable through the real execution path. Only these two bundles carry this code — I verified `bootstrap.js`, `emit.js` and `hook.js` do not reference it, so the build should leave them byte-identical; I'll commit whatever the build genuinely produces rather than hand-editing.

## 5. The implementation report

Only after the above is green: fill `implementation-report.md` from the real diff and real runs — the TDD Evidence table populated with tests that actually exist in `test/verify.test.ts`, `## Changes` describing the real diff, and `## Gates` carrying verbatim `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` output. If a gate fails, that output goes in as-is rather than a summary. Then `redkiln record-links` writes the checkpoint SHA to `story.md` (CLI-owned — I will not hand-edit item frontmatter) and the SHA goes in the Commits table.

**I will not advance the story.** The blocking finding was fabricated evidence, so the report gets authored only from observed output, and I'll report the actual gate results — including any failure — rather than a green.

Nothing in the digest needs re-litigating — I verified all of it against the tree. The plan is to do the work the spec describes, then author the report from the real diff and real gate output.

## 1. `src/store/verify.ts` — the parser rewrite (AC-001..AC-013)

**Tri-state contract.** Add `type BoundaryDeclaration = {kind:"none"} | {kind:"unparseable"} | {kind:"patterns", patterns: readonly string[]}` and change `declaredBoundary` (currently `string[] | undefined`, `:354`) to return it. Rewrite its doc comment, which today states the single-fence contract this replaces.

**Heading selection — fixes #135 (AC-001, AC-002).** Replace the single `lines.findIndex(...)` at `:358` with a collection of *every* index matching `/^#{1,6}\s+.*boundary/i`. Order candidates house-form-first: those whose heading text matches `/\b(frozen\s+)?pr\s+boundary\b/i` in document order, then the remainder in document order. Take the first candidate whose section yields ≥1 pattern. Candidates exist but none yields → `{kind:"unparseable"}`; no candidates or no `spec.md` → `{kind:"none"}` (EC-004). This is what stops a prose heading or an H1 title from voiding the real fence.

**`sectionPatterns(lines, headingIdx)`.** Section runs from the heading to the next heading of any level. **The scan must track fenced-block state** and ignore `#` lines inside a fence — otherwise AC-007's `# a comment` line reads as a heading and truncates the section mid-fence. (Today's code is accidentally immune because it stops heading-checking once it finds the fence start; the rewrite has to preserve that property explicitly.) Returns the union, document-ordered and de-duplicated, of the section's first fence and its first `Path` table (EC-005).

**`fencePatterns(body)` — fixes #129 (AC-006, AC-007).** Replaces `:375`'s `if (t !== "" && !t.startsWith("#"))`. Per line: trim; drop if empty; drop if it starts with `#` (whole-line comment, unchanged behaviour AC-007 pins); otherwise cut at the first `/\s+#/` — whitespace *then* `#`, so `allowed/a#b.md` survives intact — re-trim, drop if empty (EC-003). Fixes the trailing-comment entry that `boundaryRegExp` escapes into an unsatisfiable anchored regex.

**`tablePatterns(...)` (AC-003, AC-004, AC-005).** Find the section's first markdown table whose header row's first cell — trimmed, backticks and `*`/`_` emphasis stripped — equals `Path` case-insensitively. Any other first header cell (`Not here`, `Anchor`, `AC`) is **not** a declaration, which is what keeps the 9 negative-table specs from having prose turned into patterns. Skip the `---` delimiter row; from each body row's first cell take every backticked token via a global `` /`([^`]+)`/g `` and ignore all surrounding prose. Malformed tables (missing delimiter, ragged, no body rows) yield zero patterns and fall through to the next candidate — never throw (EC-001, EC-002).

**`boundaryCheck` (AC-008, AC-009, AC-010).** Add a `BOUNDARY_ADVISORY` constant naming both the problem and the remedy (heading present but nothing parseable; declare paths in a fenced block or a `| Path | Change |` table with backticked paths). Three arms: `none` → `{ran:false, pass:true, detail:"no boundary declared"}` byte-identical to today; `unparseable` → `{ran:true, pass:true, detail: BOUNDARY_ADVISORY}`, **never `pass:false`** (NF-003 — a hard fail would red ~100 specs); `patterns` → today's stray computation unchanged, `REDKILN_MANAGED` filter included. On the **failing branch only**, additionally compute declared patterns whose RegExp matched no changed file and append them (`; declared but matched no changed file: …`). A passing run stays quiet.

**`provenanceCheck` (AC-011, AC-012).** Change the `patterns === undefined` early return at `:713-715` to `declared.kind !== "patterns"`, so both `none` and `unparseable` stay `{ran:false, pass:true, detail:"no boundary declared"}` — the advisory is `boundary`'s job alone, and this keeps `test/verify.test.ts:976` green. It inherits both parse fixes for free, so a hijacked heading no longer voids the sha demand.

**`ledgerBlock` doc comment (AC-013).** Code untouched. Rewrite `:516`'s "Mirrors `declaredBoundary`'s heading→fence scan so the two behave consistently", which becomes false the moment this lands, to state and justify the divergence: the input is generated single-heading YAML with nothing to hijack, there is no table form of a ledger, and `#` must **not** be stripped because it is YAML's own comment syntax downstream in `parseYaml`.

Untouched per the spec: `boundaryRegExp` (#129 is an input defect, not a translation defect), `REDKILN_MANAGED`, `parseLedgerBlock`, `ledgerCheck`, `waiverOf`, `verifyIdentity` (its `spec=` digest already covers every byte read, so memoization stays correct — NF-004), and `src/cli/verify.ts`'s renderer (it already prints a `pass:true` check's detail, so the advisory is loud without a renderer change).

## 2. `test/verify.test.ts` — one failing test per AC, written Red first

Extend the existing fixture shape at `:220-250` (`"# Spec\n\n## PR boundary\n\n```\nallowed/\n```\n"` via `seedStory`/`gitBaseline`) rather than reinventing a harness; use `--json` and select the check by name where an AC asserts on `ran`/`pass`. New `describe` block alongside the AC-V-BOUNDARY / AC-PROV-* / AC-BOUNDARY-MANAGED suites:

- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-HIJACK** (AC-001): prose heading `### Where the chunk boundary comes from` above the real `## PR boundary` fence; stray change → exit 1, `err` matches `/changed outside declared boundary: .*stray/`, output does **not** contain `no boundary declared`.
- **AC-002**: H1 title containing "boundary", in-boundary change only → `boundary.ran === true && pass === true`.
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-TABLE** (AC-003/AC-004): house-style `## Frozen PR boundary` + `| Path | Change |` with `` `allowed/` ``; in-boundary → ran+pass; stray → exit 1 naming it.
- **AC-005**: negative `| Not here | Owner |` table only → advisory detail, `pass === true`, and the changed file is **not** reported stray (the assertion that catches prose-derived patterns).
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-COMMENT** (AC-006): two fixtures — `allowed/x.md   # only the CLI` and `allowed/a#b.md` — both admitted, exit 0 / no stray.
- **AC-007**: fence with a whole-line `# a comment` plus `allowed/` → in-boundary change passes *and* an out-of-boundary change still fails naming the stray (the regression pin the digest flagged as never written).
- **AC-V-BOUNDARY-ADVISORY** (AC-008): heading with prose only → exit 0, `ran === true && pass === true`, detail matches `/nothing parseable|declares nothing/`.
- **AC-009**: `templates/spec.md`-shaped spec with no boundary heading → `ran === false` and detail exactly `no boundary declared`; `AC-PROV-BOUNDARY` at `:976` stays green unmodified.
- **AC-010**: declare `allowed/` and `never-touched/`, change only a stray → failure detail contains `never-touched/`.
- **AC-PROV-HIJACK** (AC-011): AC-001 fixture + `require_commit_provenance: true` + in-boundary change + empty `links.commits` → `err` matches `/links\.commits is empty/` and `/record-links/`.
- **AC-012**: unparseable heading + flag set → `provenance.ran === false` with the exact detail while `boundary.ran === true`.
- **AC-013**: a `#`-commented YAML line inside the ledger fence still round-trips through `parseYaml`; existing AC-LEDGER-*/waiver tests stay green unmodified.

## 3. `CHANGELOG.md`

One bullet appended to the existing `### Fixed` list under `## [Unreleased]` covering #135 and #129, explicit about NF-002: the table form makes a previously-dormant check real for the 18 active `.bklg/support/**` fix-lane specs, so a fix story that strays outside its own table now reds where it previously skipped — stated so nobody reads that new red as this fix breaking the gate. `### Pack changes / migration` stays **"None."** — this ships no pack or template change.

## 4. `dist/cli.js`, `dist/index.js`

Run `pnpm build`. `dist/` is tracked here, so without the rebuild the CLI users actually run keeps the defective parse and the capability is unreachable through the real execution path. Only these two bundles carry this code — I verified `bootstrap.js`, `emit.js` and `hook.js` do not reference it, so the build should leave them byte-identical; I'll commit whatever the build genuinely produces rather than hand-editing.

## 5. The implementation report

Only after the above is green: fill `implementation-report.md` from the real diff and real runs — the TDD Evidence table populated with tests that actually exist in `test/verify.test.ts`, `## Changes` describing the real diff, and `## Gates` carrying verbatim `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` output. If a gate fails, that output goes in as-is rather than a summary. Then `redkiln record-links` writes the checkpoint SHA to `story.md` (CLI-owned — I will not hand-edit item frontmatter) and the SHA goes in the Commits table.

**I will not advance the story.** The blocking finding was fabricated evidence, so the report gets authored only from observed output, and I'll report the actual gate results — including any failure — rather than a green.

## Situation

The review is correct on every point. `git diff --stat HEAD` is empty except for a telemetry `.jsonl`; HEAD is 36c9525. All eight ACs are undelivered, the sole discharge instrument does not exist, and the submitted implementation report is falsifiable. This is a build-from-zero against the spec at `.bklg/support/fix-gate-honesty-sweep/issue-131-kb-ingest-doctor-scope/spec.md`, not a repair of partial work.

Verified anchors (exact, current): `VERIFY_DIGEST` at `:749-780` with `redkilnDoctor` at `:766`; step 1b at `:1195-1196`; the self-heal/STOP branch at `:1206-1208`; the sentence to delete at `:1209`; the retrospective line at `:1212`; the return-field list at `:1221`; the manifest projection at `:1282`. File is 1290 lines. `grep -n stash workflows/forge-kb-ingest.js` exits 1.

## Order of work (TDD, red before green)

Write `test/kb-ingest-doctor-scope.test.ts` first and capture a genuine red run against the unchanged tree, then land the workflow/relay/changelog edits, then re-run for green. The red capture is what the previous submission could not produce and is the thing that makes the report checkable.

## 1. `workflows/forge-kb-ingest.js`

**`VERIFY_DIGEST` (`:749-780`) — AC-001.** Re-describe `validate` as the scoped conjunction: `` pass | fail — the scoped verdict: `redkiln validate --kb` exited 0 AND doctorInScope is pass ``. Keep `redkilnDoctor` as the raw unscoped exit status (wording clarified to say so explicitly), since a reader must still see that the command failed. Add beside it:

- `doctorInScope: { type: 'string', description: 'pass | fail — fail iff at least one `redkiln doctor --json` problem has a `file` under the wave path set (the kbRoot the wave writes to). The GATING doctor verdict. Also fail if no JSON payload could be parsed.' }`
- `doctorOutOfScope: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'one entry per doctor problem whose `file` lies OUTSIDE the wave path set, each carrying its kind and file — recorded, never gated on' }`

`required` stays `['validate','duplicateIds','deadLinks','committed']` — NF-002 keeps the diff to one schema literal, one prompt string, two manifest keys. **Constraint:** the literal must stay interpolation-free, because AC-001's reader evaluates it with `new Function`; the descriptions therefore name the KB root in prose, never as `${KB}`.

**Step 1b (`:1195-1196`) — AC-002, EC-001, EC-002.** Command becomes `` `cd "${WT}" && redkiln doctor --json` ``. **The sentence `Record redkilnDoctor pass|fail from its exit code.` is preserved byte-for-byte, trailing period included** — `test/kb-ingest-validate-kb.test.ts:319` asserts it with `toContain`, and the spec requires that suite stay green. The scoping is appended after it: partition the JSON payload's `problems[]` by whether each problem's `file` is under `${KB}` — named as the same root the Integrate stray-path guard enforces at `:1106`, interpolated so a repo with a different `kbRoot` scopes correctly (EC-001; AC-002 asserts the root from the seed, so a hard-coded `.kb` reds). At least one in-scope problem ⇒ `doctorInScope:fail`, else `pass`; every other problem appends a `kind` + `file` entry to `doctorOutOfScope[]` and to `issues[]`. `warnings[]` continue not to gate, as `doctor` itself already excludes them from `ok`. EC-002 fallback stated explicitly: an absent or unparseable JSON payload means `doctorInScope: fail`, never "no in-scope problems" — a rule that defaults to innocence on error converts every hard failure into a pass.

**New anti-stash clause in step 1 — AC-006.** Modelled on the house register at `workflows/forge-implement.js:1259` (the spec cites `:1225`; the line has moved — I model on it and do not edit that file). Never `git stash` / `git stash -u` / `git stash pop`, because the stash stack is shared across every worktree of the repository and a concurrent session can pop an entry it did not push. Names the runnable alternative: `redkiln doctor --cwd <path-to-another-worktree-at-the-same-commit> --json`, or a throwaway `git worktree add --detach`. Both `--json` and `--cwd` are global flags (`src/cli/options.ts:151-157`), so both commands are valid. This AC reds on absence today — there is no existing stash site to change; the prompt is the only surface (EC-004 records that prose cannot bind a model, only state the rule).

**`:1206-1209` re-scoped — AC-003, AC-005.** The self-heal branch is narrowed from `If EITHER command fails` to: `redkiln validate --kb` failing **or** at least one in-scope doctor problem. The self-heal budget and STOP wording are preserved verbatim (`RE-RUN both. Do this at most twice`, `set validate:fail, committed:false, and STOP`, `do not clear intake, do not commit`) — AC-005 asserts all three, and EC-003 names over-correction as the live regression risk. A new paragraph carves out the out-of-scope case: record into `doctorOutOfScope[]`/`issues[]`, do **not** set `validate:fail`, do **not** set `committed:false`, do **not** stop — steps 2–4 proceed exactly as on a clean run; it is pre-existing repository debt this wave did not write and must not try to repair. The sentence at `:1209` is **deleted** and replaced with the scoped conjunction (`pass if redkiln validate --kb exited 0 AND doctorInScope is pass`), which does not match AC-003's forbidden `/pass ONLY if BOTH commands exit 0/`.

**Step 2 retrospective (`:1212`) — EC-005.** The `04-retrospective.md` line additionally requires that a non-empty `doctorOutOfScope[]` be named in the wave record with each entry's kind and file. Scoping is only defensible if the committed wave states what it declined to gate on. The existing `04-retrospective.md` substring stays present, keeping `AC-KBI-NO-HANDROLL`'s anti-vacuity assertion green.

**Return-field list (`:1221`) and manifest (`:1282`) — AC-004.** Add `doctorInScope`, `doctorOutOfScope` to the digest field list the prompt closes with, and project both straight through beside `redkilnDoctor` using the neighbours' fallbacks: `doctorInScope: verify?.doctorInScope || 'unknown'`, `doctorOutOfScope: verify?.doctorOutOfScope || []`. No control-flow change — same phases, same single `safeAgent` call, same `_obs` derivation, same `strayPaths` sites (NF-002).

All edits sit outside the inlined forge-lib block (`:45-398`), so `check-sync.mjs`'s byte comparison stays clean (NF-004).

## 2. `test/kb-ingest-doctor-scope.test.ts` (new)

Docblock stating the defect, the #122-independence constraint, and why each reader is read the way it is. File-local `verifyPrompt(r)` and `verifyDigest()` duplicated verbatim from `test/kb-ingest-validate-kb.test.ts:153-212` — deliberately duplicated, not imported, so the #56 suite is not coupled to this one. `run(patch?)` wraps `execute(FILE, SEEDS["forge-kb-ingest.js"], "happy", patch)` asserting `error === null` and `overran === false`.

**The harness never shells out to `redkiln doctor`.** Both failure modes are `DigestPatch` values on `label === "verify"`. This is a hard constraint, not a style choice: a test that ran `doctor` would go vacuously green the day #122 lands.

Seven describes:

- **`AC-131-DIGEST-SCOPE`** — anti-vacuity (`d.required` contains `validate`, properties contain `redkilnDoctor`, so a broken extractor returning `{}` cannot satisfy the rest for free), then both new properties present with `type` `string` / `array`.
- **`AC-131-PROMPT-SCOPE`** — `toContain("redkiln doctor --json")`, `/problems\[\]/`, `/doctorInScope/`, `/doctorOutOfScope/`, and the root asserted from the seed (`toContain(SEED.kbRoot)`) rather than hand-typed, so a prompt that stopped interpolating reds (EC-001).
- **`AC-131-PROMPT-SCOPE` (second it)** — the negative `not.toMatch(/pass ONLY if BOTH commands exit 0/)` guarded by the positive `toContain("redkiln validate --kb")` (an empty prompt satisfies any `not.toMatch`), plus `/out[- ]of[- ]scope/i`, the operative-sentence shape `/out-of-scope[\s\S]{0,200}(do NOT set validate:fail|does not gate|is NOT a blocker)/i`, and `/clear intake[\s\S]{0,120}commit/i` to pin that finalization proceeds.
- **`AC-131-MANIFEST-SCOPE`** — `outOfScopeFail` patch supplying `redkilnDoctor:"fail"`, `doctorInScope:"pass"`, non-empty `doctorOutOfScope`, `validate:"pass"`, `committed:true`, non-empty `cleared`. Asserts `committed`/`ingested` true, `_obs.outcome === "committed"`, `cleared` non-empty (regression guard against a future block-on-`redkilnDoctor` shortcut) plus the two operative new projections. Note `BASE_DIGEST` sets `committed:true` and no `cleared`, so the patch must supply `cleared` explicitly.
- **`AC-131-INSCOPE-STILL-GATES`** — (a) the three preserved gate strings plus `/in[- ]scope/i`, proving the gate is conditional rather than absolute; (b) the paired `inScopeFail` patch (`doctorInScope:"fail"`, `validate:"fail"`, `committed:false`, `cleared:[]`) asserting `committed`/`ingested` false, `_obs.outcome === "completed:uncommitted"`, `cleared` empty, `doctorInScope === "fail"`. The **pair** is the mechanism: one run cannot tell a real projection from a literal; two differing only in the digest can.
- **`AC-131-NO-STASH`** — `/never .{0,40}git stash|do NOT .{0,20}git stash/i`, `/stash[\s\S]{0,160}shared across (every |all )?worktree/i`, `/doctor --cwd/`, `/worktree/`, with the `toContain("redkiln doctor")` anti-vacuity guard.
- **`AC-131-RELAY`** — reads `commands/kb-ingest.md` from disk, whitespace-collapsed. Anti-vacuity `toContain("redkiln doctor")` and `/validate: fail/`. **Deliberate divergence, stated in-file:** the AC's literal "assert the match offset falls after `indexOf("**Verify (from inside the worktree)")`" is unsatisfiable alongside the same AC's requirement that step 6 (which precedes step 7) also carry out-of-scope language — a first-match offset check would red on correct content. I instead slice at that index and assert `/out[- ]of[- ]scope/i` and `/doctorOutOfScope|outside the wave/i` **within the step-7 slice**, which delivers the AC's stated intent (the qualification cannot be satisfied by an unrelated mention elsewhere) and is strictly stronger than an offset comparison. Step 6's blocker language is asserted separately on the pre-step-7 slice.
- **`AC-131-CHECKS`** — `expect(checkPrompts(ROOT)).toEqual([])` via direct import of the exported `checkPrompts` from `workflows/_lib/check-prompts.mjs:158` (the same dual entry point `test/assets.test.ts` uses, so the assertion is the guard itself), plus `spawnSync` of `node workflows/_lib/check-sync.mjs` and `node workflows/_lib/check-parse.mjs` asserted `status === 0` with stderr in the failure message. Those three are exactly `package.json:56`'s `check:workflows`, so this pins the whole script without shelling out to pnpm. This guard is only non-vacuous once the prompt edits land — today the assets are byte-identical to HEAD.

## 3. `commands/kb-ingest.md` — AC-007

Step 6's blocker list (`:138-139`) gains `doctorInScope: fail` and names `doctorOutOfScope[]` as explicitly **advisory, not a blocker**. Step 7's doctor bullet (`:150`) expands to state that `redkilnDoctor: fail` beside `validate: pass` and `committed: true` is an expected, correct state when the failing problems lie outside the wave's `.kb/` path set, and that the operator should read `doctorOutOfScope` to see what was set aside. Without this the operator reading a passing manifest beside a failing step-7 `doctor` re-run sees a contradiction the command never explains.

## 4. `CHANGELOG.md`

One `### Fixed` bullet at the top of the `## [Unreleased]` list (newest-first, ahead of the #130 entry), in the house shape: the defect (a repo-wide `doctor` failure the wave never wrote drove `validate:fail` → atoms authored and abandoned, `_intake` left full, `03`/`04` never written — both real waves hit this), the `${KB}` partition rule, the two new digest fields, and the anti-stash clause. **No new "Pack changes / migration" subsection** — `[Unreleased]` carries one section-level `### Pack changes / migration` reading `None.`, which already covers this change correctly: no `src/`, pack, or template file is touched.

## 5. `.bklg/support/.../implementation-report.md`

Body only — never the frontmatter (single-write-path rule). Fill the empty TDD table with one row per AC-001…AC-008 recording the real red→green transition captured against the unchanged tree before the workflow edits land; fill Changes with the actual diff summary and post-fix line numbers read from the changed file; fill Gates with results captured from real runs of `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` plus `pnpm check:workflows`. Notes records the two deviations above — the preserved `Record redkilnDoctor pass|fail from its exit code.` sentence, and the AC-007 slice-based ordering assertion — and the stale `forge-implement.js:1225` → `:1259` spec reference. **Nothing is written here that was not observed**; the previous submission's specific failure was a report describing work that did not exist.

## Not touched

No `src/` or `dist/` change (NF-001) — `redkiln doctor`, `redkiln validate --kb`, and the CLI flag roster are read as contract. `workflows/_lib/forge-lib.js` and the inlined block are untouched (NF-004). `workflows/forge-implement.js` is read as a register, not edited. `test/kb-ingest-validate-kb.test.ts` stays green unmodified — the only deletion is the `:1209` sentence, which that file does not assert on.

## Verification before reporting done

`npx vitest run test/kb-ingest-doctor-scope.test.ts test/kb-ingest-validate-kb.test.ts` (new suite green, #56 suite still green), then `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm check:workflows`. Actual output is transcribed into the report; if anything fails I say so with the output rather than reporting a pass.

- `current.gate?.kind === "command"` and its `run` matches the memoizable self-invocation shape `{{redkiln}} verify … --grain (story|integration)`. This duplicates the regex in `gates.ts:247-262` (`verifySelfInvocation`), which is private and out of the frozen boundary; the duplication gets a comment naming `gates.ts` as source of truth and is flagged in the report as the one accepted deviation;
- `opts.fresh !== true`;
- `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` unset/falsey — duplicating the three-line `disabled()` predicate from `verify-cache.ts:158-161` (also private, also out of boundary), same comment treatment;
- `declaredCommands(root, id, grain) !== null` (new import from `../store/verify.js`) **and** `verifyCacheKey({root, item: id, grain, base, commands}) !== null` — the null-probe for an unresolvable HEAD (`verify-cache.ts:113-117`). Used only as a null test, never as a key, with a comment saying so.

- right after `path`/`baseResult` are computed (~line 1050, before the dry-run return at 1057): `if (opts.preflightOnly === true && !preflightEligible(...)) return preflightResult();`
- plus a cheap guard on `verdict`/`stay` placed above the `--stay` and rejecting-verdict branches (~line 800, after `currentIndex` resolves), since those return before line 1050;
- and the real stop, after the exit gate (1157), unauthored-artifact (1183) and `requires_ac` (1207-1227) checks and before `const ts = nowTimestamp()`/`moveTo`/`emitStageEvents`: `if (opts.preflightOnly === true) return preflightResult();`.

**(e) Rewrite the stale doc comment at 748-768.** Delete the false claim that verify runs "as a CHILD PROCESS from inside this critical section" (`gates.ts:280-284` runs it in-process). "Pack changes / migration: none."

## 4. `dist/index.js`, `dist/cli.js`

It contains none of that — it is 47 lines of unauthored template shell with empty placeholder tables; grep for `cliBoth`, `stripGateSection`, `AC-001`, `30 passed`, `working tree` returns zero hits. - Add `templateDriftWarnings(root, template)`: build `rel` as `${template}.md`, find the matching DriftEntry in `listTemplateDrift(root)`, classify with `classifyDrift(entry, "template")`, and on `severity === "substantive"` return doctor's exact wording from `diagnoseTemplateDrift` (src/migrate/health.ts:915-917), prefixed with the repo-relative path to match the `<file>: <message>` shape used by adopt/doctor/validate. Entire body wrapped in try/catch returning `[]` (EC-001) so a create never becomes contingent on a secondary diagnostic.
- Add `readonly warnings?: readonly string[]` to `CreateItemResult` (currently items.ts:92-100).
- In `renderNewItem`, compute the warnings inside the existing `if (firstStage.template !== undefined)` block (the readTemplate call at :419-421) and spread onto the returned object only when non-empty, keeping the `--json` payload key-clean in the common case.

After `createItem(opts)` resolves and before the `--json`/human branch (currently :144-160), iterate `result.warnings ?? []` and write `redkiln: warning: ${warning}\n` to process.stderr. Placing it before the branch is what makes it fire in both human and --json modes and survive --quiet, per the spec.

Add a `cliBoth` helper capturing stderr alongside stdout — the existing `cli()` helper (line ~40) patches process.stdout.write only, so no stderr assertion is currently possible. Then a `describe("Fix #62: new warns on a substantively drifted pinned template")` with six named tests:
- AC-001: strip `## Gate: Discover` from `.redkiln/templates/discover.md` (the story pack's first stage is `discover`, template `discover`, produces `discover.md` — the issue's own repro), run `new story`, assert stderr contains the drift warning naming `discover.md` and the `redkiln adopt --templates` remedy.
- AC-002: same fixture — assert exit code 0 and that the rendered artifact omits the stripped section while retaining the rest (renders from the stale template, does not refuse).
- AC-003: cosmetically rewrapped template → no drift warning on stderr. Non-vacuous: `normalizeText` is `/\s+$/` with no `m` flag (trailing-only), so a mid-paragraph rewrap does register as `state: "modified"` drift and must be classified `cosmetic` by `canonicalTemplate` to stay silent.
- AC-004: pristine post-init template → no warning, existing happy paths stay green.
- AC-005: parse `--json` stdout, assert `warnings` is present and non-empty.
- AC-006: drift `.redkiln/templates/story.md` (the item-type template) only → no warning, since its `rel` cannot match `discover.md`.

One entry under the existing `[Unreleased] ### Fixed`, above the `status --json` item, describing the silent render from a drifted pinned template and the warn-never-refuse boundary, linking issue #62.

## .bklg/support/fix-core-cli-schema/issue-62-new-stale-pinned-template/implementation-report.md
Author the body from real runs: fill the TDD table per AC with observed red→green, the Changes section with the files actually touched, and Gates with actual output from `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test`. The review is accurate on every point: this is an implementation from zero, not a repair. Verified against the tree — `src/process/engine.ts:769-771` is byte-identical to the pre-fix code, `grep -rn preflightOnly src/ dist/` is empty, `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` is absent from disk and `git ls-files`, `dist/index.js:14968` still carries the old `advance()`, and the on-disk implementation report is the unfilled template.

Two findings from reading the code change how the fix must be built, because the spec's own Behavior snippet does not work as written:

1. `previewExitGate` (engine.ts:470-497) CATCHES `GateError` and returns `{pass:false, detail}`. So the spec's literal `advanceUnlocked(id, {...opts, commit:false, preflightOnly:true})` would NOT throw on a refusing gate, leaving AC-002 unmet.
2. `emitGateResult` (engine.ts:1117-1134) ALREADY returns early on `opts.commit !== true`. The spec's context-pack claim that telemetry "fires unconditionally, regardless of opts.commit" is stale. A `commit:false` pre-flight is therefore already telemetry-silent — but that also means a gate failure detected there would record nothing, losing the single `gate_result` AC-002 explicitly requires.

Both push the same way: the pre-flight must run with `commit: true` plus `preflightOnly: true`, returning before the first mutation.

## src/process/engine.ts

1. `AdvanceOptions` (line 67-115): add `readonly preflightOnly?: boolean | undefined` — documented as marking the INTERNAL outside-the-lock warming pass, explicitly distinct from `commit: false` (a user-invoked dry run), which is what preserves AC-004. Add an internal `readonly preflightBasis?: GateBasis | undefined` used only to carry the pre-flight's observed basis into the locked confirm.

2. `advance()` (769-771): restructure to
   - `if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts);` (unchanged)
   - run `advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, preflightOnly: true })` OUTSIDE the lock, capturing its returned basis
   - `return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, preflightBasis }))`
   Also rewrite the stale doc comment at 766-767: `verify` no longer runs as "a CHILD PROCESS from inside this critical section" — `gates.ts:280-284`'s `verifySelfInvocation` runs it in-process — and the comment must now describe the two-pass structure and its carve-outs.

3. Add `preflightWorthwhile()` and a stand-down / early-return branch sited around the exit-gate evaluation at line 1157. The pre-flight runs ONLY when the current stage's exit gate is the memoizable `{{redkiln}} verify --grain story|integration` self-invocation shape, and stands down (returning a non-committed result without evaluating anything) when: `opts.fresh === true`; `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` is set; `declaredCommands()` or `verifyCacheKey()` returns null (unresolvable HEAD / unidentifiable tree); or the call is a `--stay` / `--verdict` shape. These carve-outs are load-bearing, not defensive — without the `--fresh` one, `test/gate-memo-and-artifacts.test.ts:280` (`AC-MEMO-BYPASS: --fresh forces a real run`, asserting `runCount() === 2`) goes red, because pre-flight and confirm would each run for real. Same for the `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` test below it. Imports `verifyCacheKey` from `../store/verify-cache.js` and `declaredCommands`/`Grain` from `../store/verify.js` read-only; neither module is modified, honoring the frozen boundary. The self-verify shape regex is duplicated from `gates.ts`'s non-exported `verifySelfInvocation` with a cross-reference comment (gates.ts is out of boundary); worst case on drift is a stand-down, i.e. today's behavior.
   Also add one hard invariant right after `current` is computed: `preflightOnly` combined with `--stay`/`--verdict` throws, so the flag can never reach the `--stay` write path (~905) or the rejection-emit path (~991).
   The early return is placed immediately AFTER the exit-gate try/catch and BEFORE the unauthored-artifact check, so: a refusing gate emits exactly one `gate_result` (emitGateResult is live because `commit === true`) and throws before `withWriteLock` is ever called (AC-002); a passing gate returns before the passing emission at 1301, so the confirm is the only emitter (AC-003).

4. Exit-gate `emitGateResult` at line 1301: use `opts.preflightBasis ?? exitGate.basis`, carrying forward ONLY an `"evaluated"` basis. Without this, every real `--apply` would record `basis: memoized` on the confirm — destroying the field the code's own comment calls load-bearing ("a memoized or warned pass is not evidence the check ran and succeeded").

## test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts (new)

Modeled on `test/gate-memo-and-artifacts.test.ts`'s harness (temp repo, `run()` from `src/cli/index.js`, a `verify.affected_gate` script appended to `.redkiln/config.yaml`).
- AC-001: a lock-presence probe gate — the gate script records whether the write-lock directory (`lockPath(root, ".write.lock")` under the git common dir) exists at the moment it runs. Assert exactly one real execution, that it observed NO lock held, and that the confirm was a memo hit (`reusing the verified 'story' result` on stderr, `basis: evaluated` on the event).
- AC-002: failing gate — assert the thrown error keeps today's `command gate failed (EC-003)` shape, the lock directory is never created, the item file is unchanged, and exactly one `gate_result` with `pass:false` is recorded.
- AC-003: one successful `--apply` → exactly one `gate_result` event.
- AC-004: a user dry run (`advance <id> --to <stage>`, no `--apply`) writes zero telemetry events, matching today.
- AC-005: a gate script that on run 1 mutates a TRACKED source file (changing tree identity) and passes, then on run 2 exits non-zero. Asserts the confirm cache-misses, re-runs for real, blocks the write, and leaves the item's stage unchanged.
- Carve-outs: a non-memoized plain shell `run:` gate executes exactly once (no double real run); `--fresh` executes once; `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1` executes once; a repo with no resolvable HEAD executes once.
- EC-001: an unresolvable item under `--apply` surfaces the same `AdvanceError` message as today, not a gate misattribution.

There is no salvageable partial work, so this is a from-scratch implementation of the spec plus a corrected report.

## 1. `src/store/items.ts` — compute the warning

Import `listTemplateDrift` from `../migrate/drift.js` and `classifyDrift` from `../migrate/compat.js`.

Add `readonly warnings?: readonly string[]` to `CreateItemResult` (currently `id`/`uid`/`type`/`slug`/`path` at lines 92-100), documented as absent when nothing drifted.

Add a module-private `templateDriftWarnings(root, template): string[]`:
- build `rel = \`${template}.md\`` — `firstStage.template` omits the extension `readTemplate` appends, while `DriftEntry.rel` includes it;
- find the matching entry in `listTemplateDrift(root)` by `rel`; return `[]` if none;
- `classifyDrift(entry, "template")`, and only on `severity === "substantive"` emit one string;
- format as `` `${file}: ${message}` `` where `file` is `relative(root, entry.repoFile)` with backslashes normalised to `/` (reusing the idiom already at the end of `renderNewItem`), and `message` is doctor's exact `modified` wording from `diagnoseTemplateDrift` (src/migrate/health.ts:915-917): *"template '<rel>' differs SUBSTANTIVELY from the installed redkiln's bundled default — words, headings or checklist boxes changed, not just wrapping (pinned at init; `redkiln adopt --templates` to adopt the new template)"*. Packing `file: message` into one string keeps `warnings` a plain `string[]` while letting the CLI print the exact `redkiln: warning: <file>: <message>` shape AC-001 names.
- Wrap the whole body in `try { … } catch { return []; }` for EC-001, so a create never becomes contingent on a secondary diagnostic.

Note the `absent` branch is deliberately unreachable here: `readTemplate` throws `ItemCreateError` first, and `classifyDrift` returns `severity: "absent"` (not `"substantive"`) anyway — so no warning, matching the spec.

In `renderNewItem`, declare `let warnings: readonly string[] = []` before the `if (firstStage.template !== undefined)` block and assign inside it after `readTemplate` succeeds — scoping to `firstStage.template` only, never the `readTemplate(root, type)` item-file call at line 412, which is AC-006's boundary. Spread `...(warnings.length > 0 ? { warnings } : {})` into the returned object so the common quiet case stays key-clean, matching the existing optional-field idiom in this file.

## 2. `src/cli/new.ts` — print to stderr

After `const result = await createItem(opts)` and **before** the `if (flags.json === true)` branch — which returns early at line 149 and would otherwise swallow the warning — loop `for (const warning of result.warnings ?? [])` writing `` `redkiln: warning: ${warning}\n` `` to `process.stderr`. Placing it before the branch satisfies AC-001 in both modes; keeping it out of the `flags.quiet` guard means `--quiet` suppresses the human summary but not the warning, per the spec and the `record-run.ts:113` precedent.

## 3. `test/new.test.ts` — six real tests

**`fencePatterns(lines, fenceStart)` (AC-006, AC-007).** Per line until the closing fence: trim; drop empty; drop whole-line `#` (preserves today's `:375` behaviour); otherwise `const cut = t.search(/\s+#/)` and take `t.slice(0, cut)` when `cut !== -1`, re-trim, drop if empty. **`tablePatterns(rows)` (AC-003/004/005, EC-001/002).** Parse pipe rows: split on `|`, drop the leading/trailing empties, skip the `:?-{3,}:?` delimiter row. Gate on the **header's first cell** — stripped of backticks and `*`/`_` emphasis, trimmed, lowercased — being exactly `path`. Any other header (`Not here`, `Anchor`, `AC`) yields nothing, which is what keeps the 9 negative `| Not here | Owner |` specs from being read backwards into a prose-derived pattern set. From each body row's first cell take every `` `token` `` via `/`([^`]+)`/g`, ignoring surrounding prose so `` `test/` (new or existing file…) `` contributes just `test/`. ## What the review got right

Verified against the tree: `advance()` at `src/process/engine.ts:769-771` is byte-identical to the pre-fix code, `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` does not exist, `implementation-report.md` is the unfilled template, and `dist/index.js` still carries the old `advance()`. The story has zero implementation and a fabricated report. All eight issues are actionable as written, with two design corrections below.

## Two corrections to the spec's premises (found by reading the code)

**1. `preflightOnly` is not needed for telemetry suppression.** The spec's Context pack claims telemetry "fires **unconditionally**, regardless of `opts.commit`". That is false of the current code. Every emit site is already commit-gated: `emitGateResult` returns early at `engine.ts:1124` (`if (opts.commit !== true) return;`); the `--stay` verdict emit (`:941`) sits behind the `:906` dry-run return; the rejection emit checks `const commit = opts.commit === true` at `:995`; and every `emitTracked` site (`:1265`, `:1268`, `:1274`, `:1287`, `:1301`, `:1350`, `:1396`, `:1405`) sits *after* the `:1057` dry-run return. A `commit: false` pre-flight therefore already emits nothing — AC-003 and AC-004 hold without threading a flag through the emit path. I will still add `preflightOnly` (the spec's Behavior section requires the field, and I need it for reason 2), but its doc comment will state honestly that telemetry suppression is *inherited from `commit: false`*, not invented by this flag.

**2. The spec's literal one-liner does not satisfy AC-002.** The spec says `advanceUnlocked`'s dry-run path "evaluates every gate — including the command gate — and throws on failure". It does not. The dry run returns at `:1057`, *before* the real exit gate at `:1157`, via `previewExitGate` (`:470-499`) — which **catches `GateError` and returns `{pass: false, detail}` instead of throwing**, and builds its ctx as `{id, dir: located.dir}` with **no `fresh`**. Copying the spec's snippet verbatim would (a) never throw, so a blocked advance would still enter `withWriteLock` and AC-002 would silently fail, and (b) run the pre-flight while ignoring `--fresh`, then do the real run inside the lock — the exact stall the story exists to remove.

**3. The "scope amendment" the digest cites is not in the repo.** `grep` for `carve-out`/`scope amendment` across all markdown matches only `agents/redkiln-review.md` (review-agent boilerplate); it is absent from `spec.md`, `story.md`, and `project.md`. I am implementing the carve-outs regardless, because they are independently derivable and load-bearing for NF-002/NF-003 — see below. I will flag the missing amendment in the report's Notes rather than cite a document that does not exist.

## Why the carve-outs are mandatory

The memo is consulted **only** in `evaluateVerifyGate` (`gates.ts:283`), reached only when `verifySelfInvocation` matches `{{redkiln}} verify` **and** `--grain story|integration` **and** a non-empty `ctx.id` (`gates.ts:238-247`). A generic command gate (`./scripts/check.sh`) takes the `execFileSync` path at `gates.ts:295` with no memo at all. So an unconditional two-pass would run such a gate **twice for real**, with the lock still spanning the second run — strictly worse than today, and a direct NF-003 violation ("one extra *cache-hot, cheap* lookup"). The same hazard applies when `opts.fresh === true` (`gates.ts:283`), when `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` is set (`verify-cache.ts` `disabled()`), and when `verifyCacheKey` returns `null` because HEAD is unresolvable (`verify-cache.ts:113-119`, `treeIdentity`).

## `src/process/engine.ts`

- Add `readonly preflightOnly?: boolean` to `AdvanceOptions` (after `fresh`, ~`:114`). Document it as the internal-pre-flight marker: it makes the pass **throw** like a real gate evaluation and carry `fresh`, and it is *not* the telemetry switch (correction 1).
- Rewrite the stale doc comment at `:759-767`. It claims verify runs "as a CHILD PROCESS from inside this critical section" — false since `gates.ts:283` runs the verify core in-process. Replace with the real invariant: the gate is evaluated outside the lock, and the lock covers only the cache-hot confirm plus the read-modify-write.
- Restructure `advance()`:
  ```ts
  export function advance(id: string, opts: AdvanceOptions): AdvanceResult {
    if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts);
    if (shouldPreflight(id, opts)) {
      advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false, preflightOnly: true });
    }
    return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts));
  }
  ```
- Add a module-private `shouldPreflight(id, opts)` predicate returning true only when the confirm is *guaranteed* memo-servable: the current stage's exit gate is `kind: "command"` whose `run` matches `{{redkiln}} verify` with `--grain story|integration`; `opts.fresh !== true`; the `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` env is unset/falsey; `verifyCacheKey(...)` is non-null (HEAD resolvable); `opts.stay !== true` (that branch returns at `:906` before any gate, so a pre-flight is pure waste); and the transition is a **single hop** (target is the next stage). The single-hop rule is the "at most one gate per call" constraint: a `--to` walk evaluates target gates at `:1338` that the pre-flight — which returns at `:1057` — never warms, so pre-flighting a walk would leave a memo-cold heavy run inside the lock. Every failure inside the predicate is swallowed to `false`, so it can never introduce a new throw; an unresolvable item still surfaces its `AdvanceError` from the real pass exactly as today (**EC-001**).
- Thread `preflightOnly` into the `:1057` dry-run branch's `previewExitGate` call: pass `fresh: opts.fresh` in the ctx, and when `preflightOnly === true` **rethrow** the `GateError` rather than folding it into a `GatePreview`. This is what makes a blocked advance throw *before* `withWriteLock` is entered (**AC-002**). Add the `throwOnFail`/`preflight` parameter to `previewExitGate` (`:470`); its existing behavior for every non-pre-flight caller is unchanged (**AC-004**).
- No change to `gates.ts`, `verify-cache.ts`, `lock.ts`, review gates, `--stay`, or `walkToTarget`.

## `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` (new)

Modeled on `test/gate-memo-and-artifacts.test.ts` (real temp git repo, `.redkiln/config.yaml` declaring the grain's verify commands, CLI driven through `run()` from `src/cli/index.js`). The key instrument: because `evaluateVerifyGate` runs the *declared* commands, the gate stays memoizable while its command is a **probe script** that appends, per invocation, whether the write-lock directory under `<git-common-dir>/redkiln/` existed at that moment.

- **AC-001** — passing memoized gate, single-hop `--apply`: exactly one real probe invocation; the lock dir did **not** exist during it; the confirm pass is a memo HIT (`basis: "memoized"` / the "tree unchanged" notice), not a second real run.
- **AC-002** — failing gate: throws today's `GateError`/EC-003 message shape; the lock dir is **never created** (probe records absence, and no lock residue remains); exactly one `gate_result` event with `pass: false`.
- **AC-003** — one successful `--apply`: exactly one `gate_result` per gate the transition evaluates.

- **AC-005** — stale-pre-flight-write hazard: the gate's verdict depends on mutable state flipped *between* the two passes in a way that also moves the tree (the memo keys on tree identity per `verify-cache.ts:113-135`, so a tree-invisible flip legitimately hits — the test asserts the contract the cache actually offers). - **Carve-outs** — one test each: a non-memoized plain command gate, `--fresh`, `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1`, and an unresolvable HEAD (fixture repo with no commits) each run the gate **exactly once**, inside the lock, with no pre-flight and no doubled execution.

Verified against the tree: `advance()` at `src/process/engine.ts:769-771` is byte-identical to the pre-fix code, `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` does not exist, `implementation-report.md` is the unfilled template, and `dist/index.js` still carries the old `advance()`. The story has zero implementation and a fabricated report. All eight issues are actionable as written, with two design corrections below.

## Two corrections to the spec's premises (found by reading the code)

**1. `preflightOnly` is not needed for telemetry suppression.** The spec's Context pack claims telemetry "fires **unconditionally**, regardless of `opts.commit`". That is false of the current code. Every emit site is already commit-gated: `emitGateResult` returns early at `engine.ts:1124` (`if (opts.commit !== true) return;`); the `--stay` verdict emit (`:941`) sits behind the `:906` dry-run return; the rejection emit checks `const commit = opts.commit === true` at `:995`; and every `emitTracked` site (`:1265`, `:1268`, `:1274`, `:1287`, `:1301`, `:1350`, `:1396`, `:1405`) sits *after* the `:1057` dry-run return. A `commit: false` pre-flight therefore already emits nothing — AC-003 and AC-004 hold without threading a flag through the emit path. I will still add `preflightOnly` (the spec's Behavior section requires the field, and I need it for reason 2), but its doc comment will state honestly that telemetry suppression is *inherited from `commit: false`*, not invented by this flag.

**2. The spec's literal one-liner does not satisfy AC-002.** The spec says `advanceUnlocked`'s dry-run path "evaluates every gate — including the command gate — and throws on failure". It does not. The dry run returns at `:1057`, *before* the real exit gate at `:1157`, via `previewExitGate` (`:470-499`) — which **catches `GateError` and returns `{pass: false, detail}` instead of throwing**, and builds its ctx as `{id, dir: located.dir}` with **no `fresh`**. Copying the spec's snippet verbatim would (a) never throw, so a blocked advance would still enter `withWriteLock` and AC-002 would silently fail, and (b) run the pre-flight while ignoring `--fresh`, then do the real run inside the lock — the exact stall the story exists to remove.

**3. The "scope amendment" the digest cites is not in the repo.** `grep` for `carve-out`/`scope amendment` across all markdown matches only `agents/redkiln-review.md` (review-agent boilerplate); it is absent from `spec.md`, `story.md`, and `project.md`. I am implementing the carve-outs regardless, because they are independently derivable and load-bearing for NF-002/NF-003 — see below. I will flag the missing amendment in the report's Notes rather than cite a document that does not exist.

## Why the carve-outs are mandatory

The memo is consulted **only** in `evaluateVerifyGate` (`gates.ts:283`), reached only when `verifySelfInvocation` matches `{{redkiln}} verify` **and** `--grain story|integration` **and** a non-empty `ctx.id` (`gates.ts:238-247`). A generic command gate (`./scripts/check.sh`) takes the `execFileSync` path at `gates.ts:295` with no memo at all. So an unconditional two-pass would run such a gate **twice for real**, with the lock still spanning the second run — strictly worse than today, and a direct NF-003 violation ("one extra *cache-hot, cheap* lookup"). The same hazard applies when `opts.fresh === true` (`gates.ts:283`), when `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` is set (`verify-cache.ts` `disabled()`), and when `verifyCacheKey` returns `null` because HEAD is unresolvable (`verify-cache.ts:113-119`, `treeIdentity`).

## `src/process/engine.ts`

- Add `readonly preflightOnly?: boolean` to `AdvanceOptions` (after `fresh`, ~`:114`). Document it as the internal-pre-flight marker: it makes the pass **throw** like a real gate evaluation and carry `fresh`, and it is *not* the telemetry switch (correction 1).
- Rewrite the stale doc comment at `:759-767`. It claims verify runs "as a CHILD PROCESS from inside this critical section" — false since `gates.ts:283` runs the verify core in-process. Replace with the real invariant: the gate is evaluated outside the lock, and the lock covers only the cache-hot confirm plus the read-modify-write.
- Restructure `advance()`:
  ```ts
  export function advance(id: string, opts: AdvanceOptions): AdvanceResult {
    if (opts.commit !== true) return advanceUnlocked(id, opts);
    if (shouldPreflight(id, opts)) {
      advanceUnlocked(id, { ...opts, commit: false, preflightOnly: true });
    }
    return withWriteLock(opts.root, () => advanceUnlocked(id, opts));
  }
  ```
- Add a module-private `shouldPreflight(id, opts)` predicate returning true only when the confirm is *guaranteed* memo-servable: the current stage's exit gate is `kind: "command"` whose `run` matches `{{redkiln}} verify` with `--grain story|integration`; `opts.fresh !== true`; the `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE` env is unset/falsey; `verifyCacheKey(...)` is non-null (HEAD resolvable); `opts.stay !== true` (that branch returns at `:906` before any gate, so a pre-flight is pure waste); and the transition is a **single hop** (target is the next stage). The single-hop rule is the "at most one gate per call" constraint: a `--to` walk evaluates target gates at `:1338` that the pre-flight — which returns at `:1057` — never warms, so pre-flighting a walk would leave a memo-cold heavy run inside the lock. Every failure inside the predicate is swallowed to `false`, so it can never introduce a new throw; an unresolvable item still surfaces its `AdvanceError` from the real pass exactly as today (**EC-001**).
- Thread `preflightOnly` into the `:1057` dry-run branch's `previewExitGate` call: pass `fresh: opts.fresh` in the ctx, and when `preflightOnly === true` **rethrow** the `GateError` rather than folding it into a `GatePreview`. This is what makes a blocked advance throw *before* `withWriteLock` is entered (**AC-002**). Add the `throwOnFail`/`preflight` parameter to `previewExitGate` (`:470`); its existing behavior for every non-pre-flight caller is unchanged (**AC-004**).
- No change to `gates.ts`, `verify-cache.ts`, `lock.ts`, review gates, `--stay`, or `walkToTarget`.

## `test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts` (new)

Modeled on `test/gate-memo-and-artifacts.test.ts` (real temp git repo, `.redkiln/config.yaml` declaring the grain's verify commands, CLI driven through `run()` from `src/cli/index.js`). The key instrument: because `evaluateVerifyGate` runs the *declared* commands, the gate stays memoizable while its command is a **probe script** that appends, per invocation, whether the write-lock directory under `<git-common-dir>/redkiln/` existed at that moment.

- **AC-001** — passing memoized gate, single-hop `--apply`: exactly one real probe invocation; the lock dir did **not** exist during it; the confirm pass is a memo HIT (`basis: "memoized"` / the "tree unchanged" notice), not a second real run.
- **AC-002** — failing gate: throws today's `GateError`/EC-003 message shape; the lock dir is **never created** (probe records absence, and no lock residue remains); exactly one `gate_result` event with `pass: false`.
- **AC-003** — one successful `--apply`: exactly one `gate_result` per gate the transition evaluates.
- **AC-004** — a genuine dry run (`commit: false`, `preflightOnly` absent): writes no telemetry partition at all, and still returns its `gate` preview — byte-for-byte today's behavior.
- **AC-005** — stale-pre-flight-write hazard: the gate's verdict depends on mutable state flipped *between* the two passes in a way that also moves the tree (the memo keys on tree identity per `verify-cache.ts:113-135`, so a tree-invisible flip legitimately hits — the test asserts the contract the cache actually offers). Assert the in-lock confirm cache-**misses**, re-runs for real, blocks the write, and leaves the item's stage unchanged.
- **Carve-outs** — one test each: a non-memoized plain command gate, `--fresh`, `REDKILN_NO_GATE_CACHE=1`, and an unresolvable HEAD (fixture repo with no commits) each run the gate **exactly once**, inside the lock, with no pre-flight and no doubled execution.
- **EC-001** — an unresolvable item still yields `AdvanceError` with today's message shape.
- **NF-002** — a multi-hop `--to` walk behaves exactly as today (stands down from pre-flight).

## `CHANGELOG.md`

One entry under `## [Unreleased]` → `### Fixed` (subsection already exists): the cross-worktree stall, the root cause (the shared `<git-common-dir>/redkiln/` write lock spanning the command gate's shell-out), the pre-flight-then-locked-confirm fix, and — explicitly — the carve-outs under which it deliberately stands down, so the absence of the speedup for non-memoized gates reads as designed rather than broken. Pack changes: none.

## `dist/cli.js`, `dist/index.js`

Run `pnpm build` (`node scripts/build.mjs`) and commit the regenerated bundles (**NF-001**). These are the two that carry `advance()`; I'd commit whatever the build actually regenerates.

## `.bklg/support/fix-advance-write-lock-gate-scope/fix-advance-write-lock-gate-scope/implementation-report.md`

Replace the template with a report authored from **real, re-runnable output**: the filled TDD table (one row per AC/EC/carve-out, red→green), the actual checkpoint SHAs, the change summary, and the genuine gate results from `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` plus `pnpm build`. Red is established by writing the tests first against unmodified `engine.ts` — not by quoting test comments. Notes will record the three spec corrections above (the false telemetry premise, the non-throwing dry-run path, the missing scope amendment) as deliberate deviations.

**I would not advance the item past `implement`.** The prior run's fabricated report risks recording a live defect as resolved; the stage transition is the human's call once the real gates are green.","files":["src/process/engine.ts","test/advance-lock-scope.test.ts","CHANGELOG.md","dist/cli.js","dist/index.js",".bklg/support/fix-advance-write-lock-gate-scope/fix-advance-write-lock-gate-scope/implementation-report.md"]}

Nothing was implemented: history is one commit (3f3e253), the only tree change is the telemetry .jsonl, and all four workflow sites are byte-identical to the spec's pre-fix quotes. `npx vitest run test/implement-behaviour.test.ts test/implement-contract.test.ts test/workflow-model-tiers.test.ts` = 125/125, not the reported 141/141; commit 9e98b848 does not exist. So there is nothing to "repair" — the story gets implemented from scratch against the spec at .bklg/support/fix-gate-honesty-sweep/issue-130-slice-review-story-gate/spec.md, which is self-sufficient and already names every anchor.

Two grounding checks that change the shape of the work:
(a) The fabricated report is NOT on disk. implementation-report.md is the blank rendered template (empty TDD/Commits tables). Finding #8's remedy is therefore to AUTHOR the report for the first time from real evidence, not to correct a false one.
(b) RK-S0268 has landed — src/store/verify.ts:354+ now carries TABLE_ROW / HOUSE_BOUNDARY_HEADING / BoundaryDeclaration, so declaredBoundary parses the table form and prefers the house heading. The spec's ordering precondition is satisfied and the boundary leg is genuinely enforcing, so EC-004 is not a live caveat.

Method: TDD. Write each AC's test first and confirm it reds against the untouched workflow (this is the exact proof the prior report faked), then make the workflow edit and confirm green. Do the four workflow edits in one pass only after all seven ACs are red.

1. workflows/forge-implement.js — four edits, no control flow above the seal changed.
 - VERIFY_DIGEST (:784-813, AC-002): add the OPTIONAL `storyGates` array exactly as the spec's Behavior §2 gives it — items with `required: ['story', 'pass']` and properties story/pass/failedChecks/detail. Leave `required: ['story', 'gateGreen']` (:786) untouched; the optionality is load-bearing per EC-001, so an unmade claim is refused by the workflow, not rejected by the schema.
 - verifyThunk prompt (:1911-1925, AC-001): add a second numbered command block emitting one `redkiln verify --item ${s.id} --grain story --json` line per story via `slice.stories.map(...)` interpolation. Interpolate `s.id`, never `s.slug` and never a path helper (specPath/briefPath/... would trip relayViolations' PATH_HELPER and demote the relay out of haiku). Keep `Do NOT edit any code.` verbatim (the NO_EDIT predicate), keep the `affected packages` line and `RELAYING IS THE WHOLE JOB` unchanged, and attach the reason to the no-open-specs line — `redkiln verify` opens spec.md in-process, so the agent never does.
 - Pre-seal story-gate block (new, between the red-gate exit at :2073-2091 and :2096, AC-003/AC-004/EC-002): build `gateByStory` from `verify.storyGates || []`, then map `slice.stories` to failures — missing `s.id` → "no story id was seeded"; no entry → "story gate NOT REPORTED — unproven is not green"; otherwise pass only on `g.pass === true`. The `!== true` polarity is the whole point of AC-004: `=== false` would let an absent entry seal approved. Non-empty ⇒ `sealSlice(slice, 'changes-requested', storyGateFailures, sliceShas)`, `blockedAt = { slice: slice.slice, step: 'verify', kind: 'story-gate', storyGateFailures }`, `break` — mirroring :2073-2091 so it routes into the existing fix → re-review → seal tail. Placed AFTER the gateGreen loop so a red story gate never enters remediateGate (EC-003): a boundary rejection is fixed by scope judgment, not by fixing code.
 - Re-verify prompt (:2060-2062, AC-006): same per-story block. `Do NOT edit code.` already present, so NO_EDIT stays satisfied. Without this, any slice taking a remediation pass reaches the new check holding a digest never asked for storyGates and seals changes-requested for want of evidence.
 No model/effort/agentType/phase change (NF-002); gateGreen semantics, sealSlice, and the :1660-1670 skip rule untouched.

2. test/helpers/workflow-harness.ts — in digestFor's forge-implement.js branch (:155-172), add a `storyGates` entry per seeded story for `gate:` labels: `args.stories.map((s) => ({ story: s.id, pass: true }))`. In the harness, not a per-test patch — that file's own contract (:340-346) forbids using a patch to make the happy path pass, and this is what gives AC-004's `without('storyGates')` something to subtract from.

3. test/implement-behaviour.test.ts — new `AC-IMPL-STORYGATE` describe after AC-IMPL-AFFECTED (:593), five runs using the existing run()/on()/without() fixtures (:70-101) and the two-story m1 seed:
 - AC-001: `prompts.get('gate:m1')` — anti-vacuity `toContain('POST-REVIEW VERIFY')` first, then match /redkiln verify --item RK-S0001 --grain story/, the same for RK-S0002, and still `toContain('affected packages')`.
 - AC-003: patch `on(/^gate:/, …)` with RK-S0001 pass / RK-S0002 red on boundary; assert labels has `seal:m1:changes-requested` and NOT `seal:m1:approved`, `m.halted === 'stories'`, blockedAt.step 'verify', blockedAt.kind 'story-gate', and JSON.stringify(m.blockedAt) matches /RK-S0002/ and /src\/stray\.ts/. Plus the anti-vacuity unpatched run asserting `seal:m1:approved`, so an unconditional changes-requested reds.
 - AC-004: `on(/^gate:/, without('storyGates'))` ⇒ `seal:m1:changes-requested` with blockedAt naming both RK-S0001 and RK-S0002.
 - AC-005: patch the preflight digest with completedStorySlugs/completedShas and a sliceVerdicts entry carrying the story-gate finding; assert BASE has neither `resumeSlice` nor `reviewOnly` (so no escape hatch can satisfy it), then labels contains `review:m1`, no label starts with `slice:`, and `prompts.get('review:m1')` contains 'RK-S0002' and 'PRIOR REVIEW OF THIS SLICE'.
 - AC-006: patch on the exact label `gate:m1` (not the namespace) to gateGreen:false, driving one remediation attempt and leaving `gate:m1:1` green; assert labels contains `gate:m1:1`, then match the per-story command for both ids in `prompts.get('gate:m1:1')`.

4. test/implement-contract.test.ts — new describe, one source `toMatch` (the class :29-32 admits, since the stub agent ignores a schema literal): read the VERIFY_DIGEST literal by the same `match` idiom metaBlock uses (:41-47) and assert /storyGates:/, /required:\s*\['story',\s*'pass'\]/, and /required:\s*\['story',\s*'gateGreen'\]/ — the last pinning that storyGates was not made required.

5. test/workflow-model-tiers.test.ts — extend the import from workflows/_lib/scan-dispatch.mjs (:68-72) with `relayViolations` and `relayCount`, and add `it.each(workflowFiles)('%s keeps every gate: dispatch a relay', …)` beside the ceilingViolations assertion at :234: `expect(relayViolations(src, file)).toEqual([])`, with `expect(relayCount(src)).toBeGreaterThan(0)` guarding vacuity for forge-implement.js. Written as a vitest assertion deliberately — .redkiln/config.yaml declares check:workflows as `reachability_static`, which src/store/verify.ts runs at integration grain only, so a story-grain green would otherwise say nothing about the relay predicate this fix leans on.

6. CHANGELOG.md — one `## [Unreleased] → ### Fixed` entry for #130 above the current top item (#137 at :26), stating the behavior change: a slice now seals approved only after every story's `redkiln verify --grain story` is reported green, an unreported gate seals changes-requested, and NF-003's cost (N re-runs of the affected gate per slice close, moved earlier from the advance seam rather than invented).

7. .bklg/.../implementation-report.md — author the currently-blank body: the TDD table with the real red→green evidence per AC, the actual checkpoint SHAs, the files touched, and the gate results, every number reproducible by re-running against this tree. No SHA or count goes in that was not read off a command that actually ran.
